info.title: PaperPilot
info.summary: AI-powered scientific literature search across PubMed, arXiv and Crossref.

get.description:
Report liveness plus which connectors this instance has registered.

The source list is part of the health payload because the frontend uses
it to render source filters without hardcoding provider names.

get.summary: Search PubMed, arXiv and Crossref in one query
get.description: Fan out to every source, merge, deduplicate, and report per-source status.

post.description: POST variant, for abstract snippets too long to sit in a query string.

get.summary: Show how a query would be interpreted
get.description: Expose the query classifier so the UI can show the detected input type.

post.summary: Export several papers as a citation file
post.description:
Render the selected papers in the requested citation format.

Papers are looked up from the store rather than accepted in the
request body, so a citation can only be produced for a record the
server actually retrieved.

get.description: Render one paper. A GET so it can be a plain link in the UI.
Let the UI build its format picker without hardcoding the list.

schema.title: Response List Formats Api Export Formats Available Get

Author.title: Author
Author.description:
A paper author.

``given``/``family`` are kept separate whenever the source provides them
because citation formats (BibTeX, RIS) need the split. ``name`` is the
display form and is always populated.

age_seconds.title: Age Seconds
age_seconds.description: How long ago the cached response was produced.

ttl_seconds.title: Ttl Seconds
ttl_seconds.description: How long a cached response stays servable.

CacheReport.title: CacheReport
CacheReport.description:
Whether this response came from the search cache.

Reported rather than silent, for the same reason every other stage
reports: this app's whole claim is that you can see what it did. A
cache that quietly served four-minute-old results while the pipeline
panel described a fan-out that did not happen would contradict that
directly — and the age is exactly what a user needs to decide whether
to care.

ClusteringReport.title: ClusteringReport
ClusteringReport.description:
Whether clustering ran, and how it went.

Mirrors ``RankingReport``: an enrichment that did not happen is a state
the UI has to render, not an error to swallow. A result set too small
to cluster is normal, not a failure.

EnrichmentReport.title: EnrichmentReport
EnrichmentReport.description:
Whether entity extraction ran, and with what model.

Same contract as the ranking and clustering reports: the frontend
renders "entities unavailable" differently from "this paper has none".

text.title: Text
text.description: Surface form, as it appears in the text.

raw_label.title: Raw Label
raw_label.description: The label the underlying model emitted.

Entity.title: Entity
Entity.description: A distinct entity mentioned in a paper, with all its occurrences.

EntityLabel.title: EntityLabel
EntityLabel.description:
Entity categories, normalized across NER models.

Different models emit wildly different label sets — ``en_core_web_sm``
is trained on news (ORG, PERSON, GPE), while SciSpacy models emit
biomedical types (DISEASE, CHEMICAL, GENE_OR_GENE_PRODUCT). Everything
is mapped onto this enum so the API contract and the UI do not change
when the underlying model does.

EntitySpan.title: EntitySpan
EntitySpan.description: One occurrence of an entity, as character offsets into a field.

ExportFormat.title: ExportFormat
ExportFormat.description:
Formats a user can ask for.

APA and Vancouver are separate members rather than a style parameter
on one member: from the caller's point of view they are two different
things to click, and modelling them as one format with a modifier
pushes that distinction into every caller.

filename.title: Filename
filename.description: Base name for the download, without extension.

ExportRequest.title: ExportRequest
ExportRequest.description: A bulk export of previously retrieved papers.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Human-readable explanation, safe to show a user.

span.title: Span
span.description: The offending text from the summary, if localizable.

GroundingIssue.title: GroundingIssue
GroundingIssue.description: One specific, located problem found in a summary.

GroundingStatus.title: GroundingStatus
GroundingStatus.description: Outcome of checking a summary against its source abstract.

GroundingVerdict.title: GroundingVerdict
GroundingVerdict.description: The full result of checking one summary against one abstract.

IssueKind.title: IssueKind
IssueKind.description:
The specific way a summary failed to trace back to its abstract.

Kept as a closed vocabulary rather than free text so the failures can
be counted, tested, and shown in the UI as a reason rather than a
generic warning.

IssueSeverity.title: IssueSeverity
IssueSeverity.description:
Whether an issue rejects a summary or merely annotates it.

The split is earned by measurement, not taste. The lexical rules have a
0.8% false-positive rate, so a summary that trips one is almost
certainly wrong and replacing it is right.

The semantic support check is far noisier, because a genuinely
abstractive summary and a recombined claim look much alike to a
similarity threshold. Measured against live generation on 94 papers, a
threshold strict enough to catch most recombinations (0.70) cautions
**43.6%** of perfectly good summaries; the shipped 0.50 cautions 5% and
catches 61%. Blocking on a signal that noisy would destroy more good
summaries than it saves bad ones — so it annotates instead, and the
reader is told which sentence to look at twice.

id.title: Id
id.description: Stable fingerprint, derived from DOI or source id.

source.description: Provider this record was retrieved from.

summary.description: AI or extractive summary, carrying its own grounding verdict.

entities.title: Entities
entities.description: Named entities found in the title and abstract, with spans.

cluster_id.title: Cluster Id
cluster_id.description: Index of the topic cluster this paper was assigned to.

also_found_in.title: Also Found In
also_found_in.description: Other sources that returned this same work.

Paper.title: Paper
Paper.description:
A single scientific work, normalized across all sources.

Optionality is deliberate and pervasive: real-world records routinely
lack an abstract, a DOI, or a usable publication date, and the pipeline
must degrade gracefully rather than drop those records.

ParsedQuery.title: ParsedQuery
ParsedQuery.description:
The user's raw input, interpreted.

``search_terms`` is what actually gets sent to the upstream APIs: for a
pasted abstract that is a distilled keyword string, because no provider
accepts a paragraph as a query. ``raw`` is preserved untouched because
Stage 2 embeds the full text for semantic ranking.

QueryIntent.title: QueryIntent
QueryIntent.description:
What the user appears to have typed.

The four intents map onto the four input modes the product promises:
a topic, a keyword, an identifier lookup, or a pasted abstract.

RankingReport.title: RankingReport
RankingReport.description:
Whether relevance ranking ran, and with what.

Reported for the same reason source failures are: the frontend needs to
tell a user "these results are in retrieval order, not relevance order"
rather than silently presenting a worse list as if it were ranked.

semantic.title: Semantic
semantic.description: Raw cosine similarity of query and paper embeddings.

lexical.title: Lexical
lexical.description: Raw BM25 score, unbounded and corpus-relative.

rank.title: Rank
rank.description: 1-based position in the ranked result set.

RelevanceScore.title: RelevanceScore
RelevanceScore.description:
Why a paper ranked where it did.

The components are kept alongside the combined score, not discarded,
for two reasons: the UI shows a breakdown rather than an unexplained
number, and an evaluation run can attribute a ranking change to the
signal that caused it.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Restrict the fan-out; defaults to every registered source.

SearchResponse.title: SearchResponse
SearchResponse.description: Merged, deduplicated results plus the provenance of the fan-out.

SourceName.title: SourceName
SourceName.description: Identifier for an upstream literature provider.

SourceReport.title: SourceReport
SourceReport.description: Per-source diagnostics returned alongside every search.

SourceStatus.title: SourceStatus
SourceStatus.description:
Outcome of one source's contribution to a fan-out.

The frontend renders these directly: a partial result ("no results from
PubMed, showing arXiv and Crossref only") is a legitimate, informative
state rather than an error.

model.title: Model
model.description: Model or method that produced the text.

rejected_for.title: Rejected For
rejected_for.description: Why the first attempt was rejected, kept even when a retry rescued it. The final verdict says the text shown is sound; this says what it took to get there.

Summary.title: Summary
Summary.description: A paper summary, its provenance, and its grounding verdict.

SummaryOrigin.title: SummaryOrigin
SummaryOrigin.description: Where the text a user is reading actually came from.

regenerated.title: Regenerated
regenerated.description: Summaries that needed a second attempt to pass.

fell_back.title: Fell Back
fell_back.description: Summaries that could not be grounded and were replaced.

SummaryReport.title: SummaryReport
SummaryReport.description:
Per-search summarization diagnostics.

Mirrors the source, ranking and clustering reports: a stage that
degraded must say so rather than leave the UI guessing.

TopicCluster.title: TopicCluster
TopicCluster.description:
One sub-topic within a result set.

``terms`` is what makes this usable in a UI: a cluster identified only
by a number is no more navigable than the flat list it replaced, so
every cluster carries the terms that distinguish it from its siblings.
